item.title: Sundance’s ‘Take Me Home’ Turned a Personal Story Into an Anti-Ableist Creative Undertaking
item.description: Liz Sargent directs her sister Anna Sargent, who has cognitive disability, in a film that started as a Sundance short. They spoke, along with co-star Ali Ahn, about the project at IndieWire's Sundance Studio, presented by Dropbox.

item.title: Sundance 2026 Movies Sold So Far: Stephanie Ahn’s ‘Bedford Park’ Sells to Sony Pictures Classics
item.description: Moon Choi and Son Sukku star in this drama about a Korean American woman grappling with her cultural past.

item.title: Lav Diaz on ‘Magellan,’ His NYFF Joke About Casting Gael García Bernal During Sex, and Béla Tarr’s Stubborn Nature
item.description: Filipino auteur Diaz and his star García Bernal tell IndieWire about everything that went into playing Portuguese explorer Ferdinand Magellan — and the portrayal by a Mexican actor.

item.title: Are You Scared of the U.S. Government Turning on Its Own Citizens? Try 1971’s ‘Punishment Park’
item.description: Peter Watkins' controversial anti-war film is brutal to watch, but its terrifying themes haven't aged a day.

item.title: Watch Ethan Hawke Break Down the Classic Adventure Movies That Inspired ‘The Weight’
item.description: Hawke was joined by "The Weight" director Padraic McKinley and co-stars Julia Jones and Austin Amelio at the IndieWire Studio, presented by Dropbox.

item.title: ‘To Hold a Mountain’ Review: A Mother Tries to Preserve a Simple World for Her Daughter in a Sweet Portrait of Pastoral Life in Montenegro
item.description: Sundance: Directors Biljana Tutorov and Petar Glomazić depict a Montenegrin shepherd's attempt to resist the construction of a military training ground with elegance and respect.

item.title: A New Blu-ray Celebrates ‘Goodbye, Columbus’ as the Bridge Between ‘The Graduate’ and ‘Love Story’
item.description: The 1969 adaptation of Philip Roth's debut novella was a hit upon release before slowly drifting into obscurity. A new physical media release provides an opportunity for rediscovery and reappraisal.

item.title: The ‘Chasing Summer’ Team Made a Love Letter to Texas Suburbia — in St. Louis
item.description: Iliza Shlesinger, Josephine Decker, Garrett Wareing, and Tom Welling visited the IndieWire Studio, presented by Dropbox, to discuss their middle-aged coming-of-age saga.

item.title: The Cast of ‘Run Amok’ Explain How Tragic Subject Matter Affects Two Generations Very Differently
item.description: Filmmaker NB Mager and stars Molly Ringwald, Patrick Wilson, Margaret Cho, Alyssa Marvin, and Sophia Torres visited the IndieWire Studio, presented by Dropbox, to discuss turning tragedy into art.

item.title: Maria Bamford on the Best Part of Starring in Her Own Documentary: ‘Other People Are Doing Most of the Work!’
item.description: Bamford was joined by "Paralyzed by Hope: The Maria Bamford Story" co-directors Judd Apatow and Neil Berkeley in the IndieWire Studio, presented by Dropbox.
